name: Asahel
overview: Asahel was a male Levite who served as an overseer of the consecrated things under Conaniah. His role involved responsibility and stewardship within the sacred duties assigned to the tribe of Levi, reflecting a position of trust and dedication in the worship life of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Asahel means 'G-d has made,' indicating a recognition of divine creation or provision. This proper name is recorded in 2 Chronicles 31:13 and does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful theistic significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Asahel as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe entrusted with religious service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical record concerning Asahel.
scriptureSignificance: Asahel's significance lies in his administrative role overseeing consecrated items, highlighting the organized and reverent management of sacred duties in Israel's worship system. His service under Conaniah underscores the structured leadership within the Levites during the period described in 2 Chronicles. This reflects the biblical emphasis on faithful stewardship and order in the service of the Lord.
